comment: Authored geometry for the ten planet surfaces (Phase 9, decision D4). Written by scripts/make-planet-glb.mjs; the .glb is reproduced byte for byte by re-running it, and scripts/tests/planet-assets.test.mjs holds every number below against the file on disk. The mesh's NAME IS A PROP KIND - not a material key, because every prop family on a planet already draws in one shared material (PlanetWorld._propMaterial) so a material name would say nothing. src/worlds/planets/PlanetAssets.js reads the kind off the mesh, discards the glTF material unread, and PlanetProps.geometryFor SUBSTITUTES the geometry inside the field's existing InstancedMesh. Nothing is added: no renderable, no instanced mesh, no draw call, no material, no shader program, no light, no collider - which is a stronger position than the belt's hero rock could take, because there every boulder was not the same case and a fourth bucket had to be bought. Which boulders use it is the descriptor's own word for what the thing is, kind: 'boulders' - all 8,880 of them across thirteen fields on nine of the ten planets. A file missing at runtime degrades to IcosahedronGeometry(1, 0) at the same twenty triangles in the same places with the same colliders - see PlanetAssets.js - and that is the arm the whole headless suite takes.

assets.source: scripts/make-planet-glb.mjs - procedurally authored in this repository, 2026-08-24
assets.note: A unit-radius ejecta block at exactly the twenty triangles of the IcosahedronGeometry(1, 0) it replaces, so the substitution is free in every axis the budget measures. Three octaves of deterministic value noise on the radius, biased inward so the body has bays rather than bulges, and two seeded clipping planes on non-opposed axes. The planes buy ASYMMETRY, not a fracture face: at this tessellation a 37-degree cap cannot contain two of twelve vertices that are 63.4 degrees apart, so at most one vertex is ever clipped and no two facets come out coplanar - measured off these bytes, where the most nearly parallel face pair is dot 0.877 against a regular icosahedron's 0.7947, and pinned by a negative assertion in planet-assets.test.mjs. Every face carries its OWN UV island at a seeded offset AND a seeded rotation. Both halves matter: the polyhedron UVs it replaces pinch to a point at the poles and seam down the lit face, and an island scheme without the rotation is worse still - it lines the anisotropic prop texture up across facet boundaries into ladders, which photographed as a paved terrace. Facet areas span 1.40x; an unmodified icosahedron spans 1.00x. The radial envelope stays inside the 1.0 the icosahedron reaches, so the drawn block spills no further outside its own collider than it already did.
